最近硅谷两大佬因为马斯克吵翻了，结果老马亲自下场，一句话把全网看乐了。 先是著名反垄断评论家 Matt 泼冷水：SpaceX 算什么奇迹？马斯克根本不是天才，无非是会找华尔街搞钱，用钞票和工程师硬堆出来的。 这话连平时谁都不服的硅谷传奇程序员 DHH 都看不下去了，直接回怼：太酸了！哪怕你不喜欢马斯克，也得承认他“把吹过的牛变成现实”的能力举世无双。从特斯拉、脑机接口到 SpaceX，世上有一百万个会搞钱的投资人，但只有一个马斯克。 随后马斯克本尊下场，只回了一句灵魂反问：“行，那你给我解释一下蓝色起源、波音和 ULA？” 这一刀，直接捅在了“唯金钱论”的肺管子上。 如果光靠砸钱就能上天，那现在的太空霸主绝不可能是 SpaceX： 1、 比谁更有钱？ 贝索斯的蓝色起源比 SpaceX 早成立两年，背后站着前世界首富，从来不缺钱，结果到现在还在努力追赶。 2、 比谁补贴多？ NASA 当年搞载人航天，同一个任务，给波音砸了 42 亿美元，给 SpaceX 只给了 26 亿。结果 SpaceX 从 2020 年就开始像公交车一样送宇航员上天，波音的飞船却连宇航员都接不回来，最后还得靠 SpaceX 去救场。 3、 比华尔街输血？ SpaceX 起步根本没有华尔街一分钱，全是马斯克卖掉 PayPal 后自己掏的 1 亿美元家底。猎鹰 1 号连炸三次后差点破产，第四次才绝处逢生。 DHH 说得太对了：钱能买来顶级工程师，但买不来“不怕炸火箭”的魄力。 看看星舰第 15 次试飞（Flight 15）就懂了：同一个任务里，助推器在海里丢了，但飞船却从轨道返航、被发射塔的“机械筷子”稳稳夹住。 放在传统航天巨头那里，“丢了助推器”这半句话，就够他们停飞开两年的事故批斗会了；但在 SpaceX，这只是通往成功的又一组实验数据。 @elonmusk 说实话，到底哪个更难造：是一枚能上天的火箭，还是一家“允许工程师靠炸火箭来试错”的公司？

What was the significance of this weekend's SpaceX tower catch: "Catching the second stage is substantially harder than catching the first stage because the Ship returns from orbit while the booster returns from a short suborbital hop. The booster separates minutes after liftoff, performs a brief boostback, and comes back from only a few hundred kilometers away at relatively low speed. Ship must reach orbital velocity, deploy payload, coast for many hours, execute a precise deorbit burn, survive full reentry heating, and only then perform its landing burn. As such, Ship must carry a functional heat shield, fly a long guided atmospheric trajectory from the other side of the planet, and execute a high-energy flip into the “chopsticks” while protecting its heat-shield side. Those combined demands of orbital energy, thermal protection, long-range guidance, and final precision are why a Ship catch is so incredibly difficult. No prior system, including the Space Shuttle, recovered a rocket-style orbital stage in this manner. The catch validates the path to full reusability which is the foundation of Starship’s cost and cadence targets. This is particularly important in driving the economics of orbital data centers." - DB

Well, most of the time projections are noise and reactionary. Like right now, sky-high projections for $ANT $700-$800B ARR over next few years is stirring up hype that I'd argue gets revised down later. I do think it's important to model in capex forecasts dropping past 2028, due to the current reflexive nature of AI selloffs, rate hikes, etc. The drawn out duration of Iran War doesn't help, Jensen leaving $NVDA certainty draws concerns over Nvidia's ecosystem. But any catalyst, like if Iran War ends, can also change sentiment in a heartbeat (since bearish positioning is overwhelming). - It's also clear financing has been tightening, since OpenAI only managed to raise $11B of their original $30B target so far. - Markets are reacting enthusiastically to companies like $TE doing a $100M ATM today (nuking valuations) - Although the "guppy" sector is probably the most sensitive to financing + rate changes. On bright side... Neoclouds like $NBIS or $IREN seem to be adjusting by getting 100% capex prepayments or 90% GPU prepayments from their counterparties. What I'd argue though is lower aggregate capex does not apply uniformly in supply chains. - Mid-high range lasers for NPO/CPO are still sold out, as seen with $LITE now starting negotiations for 2030 capacity. - MLCCs are seeing further tightening as content usage goes up for AI servers - ABF substrates to InP substrates not really going anywhere. If content per system goes up 10X-15X, capacity expands at 2-3X Y/Y, and capex drops 28%. And content is so cheap that you can triple order and screw over competitors with wafer supply... I'm pretty confident you'll see acceleration upstream in bottlenecks from optical components to substrates despite potential aggregate capex dropping. Another rant is: -I keep seeing this argument that "low P/E is a warning for cyclical that's going to crash" but these are just clown takes Nobody seems to analyze duration scenarios like capacity expansion vs. content changes vs. demand. to actually see how long those earnings last. If everyone seems to be exiting DDR2 lines, there's probably going be more tightness in 2027 despite consume demand weakening, even if it looks like it's low P/E. - Also for concerns about CPO "delays", the same components like lasers are used for NPO. You'll still see 150-200mW NPO lasers or ELS NPO using the same 300–400+ mW lasers as CPO. We'll just see acceleration with NPO as a bridge if CPO gets delayed and higher range lasers likely to remain in a severe shortage. - Feels like markets have also completely discredited the merit of take/pay price floor LTAs as well that companies like SK Hynix to Samsung have. If contractual agreements hold up, memory players look very undervalued. TLDR: - I think it's important to model in capex decreasing to numbers like -30% in hypothetical downside sceanrios. Given AI profitability, it's clearly not sustainable for hyperscalers to aggregately increase capex $500B or $1T+ Y/Y, and that's never been a case I've argued. - This is also not the same thing as demand destruction that markets are overreacting to now (which haven't happened yet). - We can see demand revisions for GPUs, ASICs, and heavier cost parts of the supply chain, while acceleration increases elsewhere. The nuances market miss by indiscriminately selling everything is going to present compelling opportunities when the dust settles. I think in the end institutions are probably going to end up owning more of the same names retail discovered early on. Anyway, I think it's a good idea to try and survive until more earnings comes out.

The first two features Matt Palmer walks through in his What's new in Grok Bot 1.0 video this morning, Team Bot improvements and bots that join your meetings, are the same two things I asked for right here on X. On August 30 I wrote that we need to be able to share Grok Bots across teams, and Elon replied "Coming soon." On October 25 I suggested the Grok Bot team let my bot join a Zoom or Teams call with me, or for me, and Elon replied "This might be possible." Meetings started switching on for users less than two weeks later, and now both features lead the 1.0 release. That says a lot about how responsive this team is. A user describes a need, Elon weighs in himself, and within weeks it is in the product and getting better. Any bot can now become a Team Bot at the flip of a switch, you choose exactly who it is shared with, and a new analytics tab shows the hours it has saved. In a meeting, the bot listens, answers in the chat and picks up spoken instructions, pulling what you need from your connected tools while the meeting is still going. The tempo of Grok Bot's evolution is extraordinary. And these are only two of the many new features in 1.0, so watch Matt's video to see just how fast Grok Bot is improving. I'm grateful to Matt, the team and Elon for listening. My original asks: https://t.co/ptwIwyUnmI and https://t.co/S84sN2CbZu

Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions: 1. Order visibility and shipment plans: Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28). (1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic. (2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases. (3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic. 2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes: v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order. (1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled. (2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year. (3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials. 3. Market attention and supplier outlook: Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus. (1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it. (2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source. (3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

Google TPU 重點更新：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 新訂單推升出貨能見度至 2029 年、v10 產品線大幅調整 (改為 Quillfish)、聯發科與 Broadcom 為供應商中之領先關注焦點 我最新的產業調查與研究結論： 1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃： 受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。 (1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。 (2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。 (3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。 2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整： v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。 (1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。 (2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。 (3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。 3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望： 近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。 (1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。 (2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。 (3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU 營收將超越 TPU。
